Knut Hamsun, Hunger, translated by George Egerton.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/knut-hamsun/hunger/george-egerton

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Knut Hamsun, the author, died 1952 (Wikidata Q40826, P570 = 1952-02-19).
- George Egerton, the translator, died 1945 (Wikidata Q273207, P570 = 1945-08-12).

First publication of the text used: 1899 for the English text (the original was published in 1890). SE colophon: 'Hunger was published in 1890 by Knut Hamsun. It was translated from Norwegian in 1899 by George Egerton.'

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1899, before 1931, and the edition's rights statement (quoted below) places it in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (not stated in the facts; for the English text the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa; for the Norwegian original, Norway): each has a copyright term of life plus 70 years or less. The last person to die died in 1952, so the work is in the public domain in each of them no later than 1 January 2023.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: Hunger was published in 1890 by Knut Hamsun. It was translated from Norwegian in 1899 by George Egerton.
- Wikidata Q40826 (Knut Hamsun), P570 = 1952-02-19.
- Wikidata Q273207 (George Egerton), P570 = 1945-08-12.
